questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A man obtained a bid of $10,000 to tear down an old structure on his newly purchased farm and another bid of $90,000 to replace it with a structure in which the man planned to house a new herd of dairy cows. Having only limited cash available, the man asked his uncle for a $100,000 loan. The next day, the man's uncle in a signed writing promised to lend the man $100,000 repayable over 10 years in equal monthly installments at 10% annual interest. The man promptly accepted the demolition bid and the old structure was removed, but the uncle thereafter refused to make the loan. Despite diligent efforts, the man was unable to obtain a loan from any other source.
In a successful claim for monetary relief against the uncle based on promissory estoppel, what is the probable measure of the man's recovery?

choices.A: Expectancy damages, measured by the difference between the value of the new structure and the old structure, less the amount of the proposed loan ($100,000).
choices.B: Expectancy damages, measured by the estimated profits from operating the dairy farm for 10 years, less the cost of repaying a $100,000 loan at 10% interest over 10 years.
choices.C: Nominal damages only, because both expectancy and reliance damages are speculative.
choices.D: Reliance damages, measured by the $10,000 expense of removing the old structure, adjusted by the decrease or increase in the market value of the man's land immediately thereafter.

questions.explanation:
Promissory-estoppel damages
Reliance
  • Intended to put enforcing party in same position as if promise had not been made
  • Measured by out-of-pocket expenses incurred by enforcing party in reliance on promise
Expectation
(rare)
  • Intended to put enforcing party in same position as if promise had been performed
  • Measured by nonspeculative expectation of enforcing party

Promissory estoppel allows a party to recover damages stemming from another's failure to perform a promise when no valid contract exists. However, such damages may be limited as justice requires. This typically leads to an award of reliance damages based on the out-of-pocket expenses incurred by the enforcing party. This is designed to place the enforcing party in the same position as if the promise had never been made and to avoid unjust enrichment of the enforcing party.

However, in some promissory-estoppel cases, courts have awarded expectation damages. Expectation damages are designed to put the enforcing party in the same position as if the promise had been performed. These damages usually exceed reliance damages but cannot be speculative—eg, the value of a nonexistent building, estimated profits from a nonexistent farm (Choices A & B).

Therefore, the probable measure of the man's recovery is reliance damages, measured by the expense of removing the old structure in reliance on the uncle's promise ($10,000). This amount should then be adjusted by the decrease or increase in the market value of the land after demolition to further compensate the man for losses or avoid his unjust enrichment, respectively.

(Choice C) Nominal damages (eg, $1) may be awarded when no reliance or expectation damages can be shown. But here, the man's reliance damages of $10,000 can be shown, so an award of nominal damages is inappropriate.

📌 Educational Objective

Damages for promissory estoppel may be limited as justice requires. This typically results in an award of reliance damages based on the claimant's out-of-pocket expenses, but some courts have awarded expectation damages to put the claimant in the same position as if the promise had been performed.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 90 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (damages for promissory-estoppel claim).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子为其新购农场上的一座旧建筑的拆除工程获得了一份10,000美元的报价，并为原地新建一座计划用于饲养新奶牛群的建筑获得了另一份90,000美元的报价。由于手头现金有限，该男子向其叔叔请求一笔100,000美元的贷款。第二天，该男子的叔叔以书面形式签署文件，承诺向该男子出借100,000美元，该笔贷款将在10年内以10%的年利率按月等额分期偿还。该男子随即接受了拆除报价，旧建筑被拆除，但其叔叔此后拒绝提供贷款。尽管尽了最大努力，该男子仍无法从任何其他渠道获得贷款。

在基于允诺禁反言原则向其叔叔成功提起的金钱救济索赔中，该男子可能获得的赔偿额度是多少？

zh-choices.A: 预期损害赔偿，其计算方式为新建筑的价值与旧建筑的价值之差，再减去拟议贷款的金额（100,000美元）。
zh-choices.B: 预期损害赔偿，其计算方式为经营奶牛场10年的预估利润，减去在10年内以10%利率偿还100,000美元贷款的成本。
zh-choices.C: 仅名义损害赔偿，因为预期损害赔偿和信赖损害赔偿都具有不确定性。
zh-choices.D: 信赖损害赔偿，其计算方式为拆除旧建筑所花费的10,000美元费用，并根据此后该男子土地市值的增减进行调整。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Remedies - Promises Binding Without Consideration

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：允诺禁止反言（promissory estoppel）的救济通常先看信赖损失，不是直接给你最会赚钱的期待利益。

三秒认题路径：

无对价 → 书面承诺 → 先拆旧房 → 贷款反悔 → 看信赖赔偿

核心法律规则

这题只抓这一条

允诺禁止反言（promissory estoppel）是：没有有效合同，但一方因相信承诺而行动，法院可以按“衡平所需（justice requires）”限制赔偿。考场上通常给的是信赖损失（reliance damages），也就是把你放回“如果这句话根本没说过”的位置。

期待损失（expectation damages）只有少数时候才会给，而且必须是不靠猜的、能算出来的收益；像“还没建成的牛舍值多少钱”“未来十年奶牛场利润多少”这种，考试里一般直接判成太虚。

核心判例：Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 90 — 允诺禁止反言的赔偿通常以信赖损失为主，期待损失只是例外，且不能靠猜。

思维导图

先问：题目是在算“承诺没兑现后的赔多少”吗？
是，但先看类型：没有有效合同，靠的是 promissory estoppel。
规则起点：默认给 reliance damages，把人拉回到“没听信承诺之前”。
本题触发事实：他已经花了 $10,000 拆旧结构，这就是可见的 out-of-pocket loss。
卡死点：不能把“未来牛舍利润”或“新旧建筑价值差”直接拿来算，因为那是 expectation damages，太猜。
结论：先算拆房费用，再按土地拆除后价值变化微调，答案落在 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：叔叔答应借钱后，男人本来要做的是一个能赚钱的奶牛场，所以应该直接赔“未来利润”。

但考试真正问的是：承诺没兑现时，法院通常先补你已经掏出去的钱；司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这题里真正能稳稳证明的，是拆旧房的 $10,000，不是未来经营收益。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干最稳的损失是 拆除旧结构的 $10,000，这正是信赖损失；再按土地价值变化微调，才能避免多赔或少赔。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把新旧建筑价值差当成既定收益了，value 还没变成可赔项目。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间收益误判

✕ B: 直接算十年奶牛场利润，命题人就是在骗你把 profits 当成确定值。

❌ 事实误判 | 赔偿基础漏读

✕ C: 说没有可赔损失，但题干明明给了 $10,000 的实际支出。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓已发生的口袋支出，再判断有没有把它偷换成不确定的未来利润。

考场速记

记住一句：允诺禁止反言先看信赖，只有少数情况下才碰期待；能算出来的花费先赔，猜出来的利润先放下。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A seller entered into an agreement to sell a machine to a buyer for $5,000. At the time of the order, the buyer gave the seller a down payment of $1,000. The buyer then built a foundation for the machine at a cost of $250. The seller failed to deliver the machine.
The buyer made reasonable efforts to find a similar machine and bought one for $5,500 that did not fit on the foundation. The buyer sued the seller for breach of contract.
Which of these amounts claimed by the buyer, if any, could best be described as restitution?

choices.A: The $250 cost of the foundation.
choices.B: The $500 difference in price.
choices.C: The $1,000 down payment.
choices.D: None of the claimed amounts.

questions.explanation:
Restitutionary damages
Definition
  • Damages awarded to restore to claimant the value of whatever benefit was conferred upon recipient
Purpose
  • Prevent unjust enrichment
Measure
  • Reasonable value of work performed or services rendered (ie, cost of recipient obtaining comparable performance)
  • If applicable, extent to which recipient's property has increased in value or recipient's other interests have been advanced

Restitutionary damages are awarded to restore to a contracting party the value of any benefit conferred on the other party. Under the UCC, where the seller fails to deliver the promised goods or the buyer rightfully rejects the goods, the buyer is entitled to the return of any payment made on the goods as restitution.

Here, the buyer paid the seller a $1,000 down payment for a machine that the seller failed to deliver. As a result, the $1,000 down payment is the amount that could best be described as restitution (Choice C).

(Choices A & B) Neither the $250 cost of the foundation nor the $500 difference between the contract price of the seller's machine and the price of the substitute machine (ie, cost of cover) conferred a benefit on the seller (not restitution).

📌 Educational Objective

Where a seller fails to deliver the promised goods or the buyer rightfully rejects them, the buyer is entitled to the return of any payment made on the goods as restitution.

UCC = Uniform Commercial Code

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 344 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (purpose of remedies).
  • U.C.C. § 2-711 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (buyer's remedies in general).
  • U.C.C. § 2-713 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (buyer's damages for nondelivery/repudiation).
questions.zh-question:
一名卖方与一名买方签订协议，以5000美元的价格向其出售一台机器。下订单时，买方向卖方支付了1000美元的定金。随后，买方为该机器建造了一个地基，花费了250美元。卖方未能交付该机器。

买方付出了合理的努力去寻找一台类似的机器，并以5500美元的价格购买了一台，但这台机器与所建地基不匹配。

买方以违约为由起诉了卖方。

买方索赔的这些金额中（如有），哪一项最能被描述为返还财产（restitution）？

zh-choices.A: 建造地基的250美元成本。
zh-choices.B: 500美元的差价。
zh-choices.C: 1000美元的定金。
zh-choices.D: 以上皆非。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Remedies - Restitution and Reliance Recoveries

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：卖方违约后，买方能拿回的是自己给对方的利益，还是自己为履约支出的成本。

三秒认题路径：

卖方未交货 → 找返还利益 → 看谁受益 → 只返对方所得 → 选定金

核心法律规则

返还性损害赔偿（restitutionary damages）的考场意思：把一方因合同从对方那里拿走的利益还回去，防止 不当得利（unjust enrichment）。

在 买卖合同（UCC sale of goods）里，如果卖方未交货，买方通常可以要求返还自己已付给卖方的款项；这类钱是卖方已经拿到的利益，所以属于 restitution。

但买方自己去做的地基成本、或后来另买替代机器多付的价差，都是买方自己的支出，不是卖方收到的利益，所以不算 restitution。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 344 与 U.C.C. § 2-711 的组合规则锁定本题：卖方违约时，买方可取回已付给卖方的价款。

思维导图

1. 谁拿到利益
卖方已经收到 $1,000 预付款。
2. 谁在花钱
地基 $250 是买方自己的支出，没给卖方带来利益。
3. 替代购买差价
多付的 $500 属于 cover / expectation，不是返还对方所得。
4. 结论
能返还的只有卖方实际取得的利益，所以答案锁定 定金。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：foundation cost 和 cover 也是因为违约才花出去的，所以都能要回来。

但考试真正问的是：这笔钱有没有先跑到卖方口袋里；没有的话，它更像 expectation damages 或 reliance damages，不是 restitution。

司法考试看的是「对方有没有拿到利益并该吐回来」，而不是「你后来有没有多花钱」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里卖方已经拿到 $1,000 down payment 却未交货，这笔钱就是卖方受领的利益，最像 restitution。

❌ 事实误判 | 地基当成返还

✕ A: 把 $250 当成卖方得利了，但这只是买方自己先垫的钱。

❌ 法律适用 | 差价规则错位

✕ B: 把 cost of cover 误当返还，它是补履约利益，不是吐回对方所得。

❌ 概念混淆 | 返还对象看错

✕ D: 以为没有可赔的项，但定金本身就是卖方已经取得的可返还利益。

这题建议用什么方法？

先问“钱有没有流到对方手里”，再分清 restitution 和 expectation / reliance。

考场速记

记住一句话：restitution 只追“对方拿走了什么”，不追“你自己后来多花了什么”。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A high-volume pleasure-boat retailer with a nearly inexhaustible supply of boats entered into a written contract with a boater, signed by both parties, to sell him a power boat for $12,000. The manufacturer's price of the boat delivered to the retailer was $9,500. As the contract provided, the boater paid the retailer $4,000 in advance and promised to pay the full balance upon the boat's delivery. The contract contained no liquidated damages provision.
Prior to the agreed delivery date, the boater notified the retailer that he would be financially unable to conclude the purchase; and the retailer thereupon resold the same boat that the boater had ordered to a third person for $12,000 cash.
If the boater sues the retailer for restitution of the $4,000 advance payment, how should the court decide?

choices.A: The boater's claim should be denied, because, as the party in default, he is deemed to have lost any right to restitution of a benefit conferred on the retailer.
choices.B: The boater's claim should be denied, because, but for his repudiation, the retailer would have made a profit on two boat-sales instead of one.
choices.C: The boater's claim should be upheld in the amount of $3,500 ($4,000 minus $500 as statutory damages under the UCC).
choices.D: The boater's claim should be upheld in the amount of $4,000 minus the amount of the retailer's lost profit under its contract with the boater.

questions.explanation:
Breaching buyer's recovery of advance payment (UCC § 2-718)

Buyer who made advance payment before breach can recover amount paid minus seller's:

  • liquidated damages – amount set forth in contract
  • statutory damages – 20% of contract price or $500, whichever is less (if no valid liquidated damages clause)
OR
  • actual damages – expectation damages plus any incidental damages (if amount exceeds statutory damages)
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.

Under the UCC, a breaching buyer is entitled to restitution damages for the value of any advance payments it made to the seller. This ensures that the seller is not unjustly enriched at the buyer's expense (Choice A). However, the buyer's damages award will be offset by the seller's damages. If, as here, there is no liquidated damages provision, then the seller's offset is the greater of the following:

  • Statutory damages – $500 or 20% of the total contract price, whichever is smaller
  • Actual damages – expectation damages (eg, lost profits if the seller is a lost-volume seller), plus any incidental damages (eg, shipping or transportation costs)

Therefore, an injured seller is not limited to a $500 statutory offset when the seller's actual damages exceed that amount (Choice C).

Here, the retailer is a lost-volume seller, as evidenced by its nearly inexhaustible supply of boats. But for the boater's breach, the retailer would have made two sales (and two profits) rather than one. As a result, the retailer's actual damages are its lost profit from the sale to the boater plus incidental damages (none are indicated). The boater's claim should therefore be upheld in the amount of $4,000 for the advance payment minus the amount of the retailer's lost profit.

(Choice B) The retailer would have made a profit on two boat sales instead of one had the boater not repudiated the contract. However, since the boater is entitled to restitution of the $4,000 advance payment, the retailer's lost profit (from the sale to the boater) will be subtracted from—but not negate—the boater's claim.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the UCC, a breaching buyer is entitled to restitution damages for the value of any advance payments it made to the seller, minus the amount of the seller's damages.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-718 (Am. Law Inst. & Unif. Law Comm'n 2020) (liquidation or limitation of damages and deposits).

一家拥有几乎无限船只供应的高销量游艇零售商，与一名船夫签订了一份由双方签字的书面合同，以12,000美元的价格向其出售一艘摩托艇。制造商交付给零售商的船只价格为9,500美元。根据合同规定，船夫向零售商预付了4,000美元，并承诺在船只交付时付清余款。该合同不包含违约赔偿金条款。

在约定的交付日期之前，船夫通知零售商，他因经济原因无法完成购买；零售商因此将船夫订购的同一艘船以12,000美元现金转售给第三方。

如果船夫起诉零售商，要求返还其4,000美元的预付款，法院应如何判决？

zh-choices.A: 船夫的诉求应被驳回，因为作为违约方，他被视为已丧失要求返还其给予零售商的利益的任何权利。
zh-choices.B: 船夫的诉求应被驳回，因为若非他拒绝履行合同，零售商本可以从两笔船只销售中获利，而不是一笔。
zh-choices.C: 船夫的诉求应被支持，金额为3,500美元（即4,000美元减去UCC规定的500美元法定损害赔偿金）。
zh-choices.D: 船夫的诉求应被支持，金额为4,000美元减去零售商根据其与船夫的合同所损失的利润金额。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Remedies - Remedies

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：违约买方（breaching buyer）先付了定金后又毁约，能不能拿回 预付款（advance payment），答案是“能拿回，但要先扣掉卖方的损害赔偿”。

三秒认题路径：

先付钱 → 买方毁约 → 卖方再卖掉 → 看返还减额 → 选 D

核心法律规则

UCC 2-718 的考场规则

在 UCC § 2-718 下，违约买方通常可以要回已经付给卖方的款项，因为法律不想让卖方白白拿走买方的钱。可是这不是“全额无条件返还”，而是要先扣掉卖方的损失；如果合同没有有效的 liquidated damages（约定损害赔偿） 条款，卖方可以用法定扣减或实际损害赔偿来抵扣。

这里真正要算的是：买方先拿回 restitution，再减去卖方因为这笔交易少赚的利润。卖方如果是 lost-volume seller（失去成交量的卖方），它的 actual damages（实际损害） 往往就是这单本来能赚到的利润，而不是只卡在一个固定的 $500。

核心判例： UCC § 2-718 的规则本身就是本题锁定答案的关键：买方可返还预付款，但要减去卖方的损失；卖方不是只能拿到象征性的法定扣减。

思维导图

1. 买方先付 $4,000
advance payment 已经交出去，所以先有可返还的利益。
2. 买方先毁约
他在交货前通知无法完成购买，触发 breach，但不等于自动没收全部预付款。
3. 卖方又卖掉同一艘船
这说明卖方是 lost-volume seller，不是“卖一次就满了”的普通卖家。
4. 先走返还
买方可以先主张 restitution，核心不是惩罚，而是防止卖方白赚预付款。
5. 再看抵扣
卖方的 lost profit 要从返还额里扣掉，结果不是全额 $4,000，也不是只剩 $500。
6. 结论
结论：$4,000 - 卖方利润损失 = 选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：买方都先违约了，那他是不是就把钱全丢了，或者卖方只能拿到一个固定的 $500 扣减。

但考试真正问的是：restitution 不是“白拿回全部”，而是“先返还，再扣卖方损失”；这里卖方是 lost-volume seller，所以可扣的是实际利润损失，不是机械卡死在 $500。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干有 $4,000 预付款，又有卖方把同一艘船卖出，说明买方可先拿回款项，但要扣掉卖方的 lost profit。

❌ 概念混淆 | 默认没收误判

✕ A: 你把“违约”直接等于“全部没收”，忽略了 restitution 这一步。

❌ 事实误判 | 两次成交误判

✕ B: 你只盯着“卖了两次”，却没算买方仍可先收回 advance payment。

❌ 法律适用 | 法定封顶误判

✕ C: 你把 $500 当成硬上限，但卖方的实际利润损失更高时，抵扣就不止这点。

这题建议用什么方法？

先确认买方能否返还，再看卖方是普通卖家还是 lost-volume seller，最后用实际损失去扣。

考场速记

记住一句话：违约买方可以拿回预付款，但要减去卖方损失；如果卖方还能证明自己本来还能多赚一单，就别死记 $500。

口诀：“先返还，再扣损失；有利润损失，就不是白送。”

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A seller and a buyer, standing on a 10-acre tract of land, orally agreed to its sale and purchase for $5,000, and orally marked its bounds as "that line of trees down there, the ditch that intersects them, the fence on the other side, and that street on the fourth side."
In which of the following is the remedy of reformation most appropriate?

choices.A: As later reduced to writing, the agreement by clerical mistake included two acres that are actually beyond the fence.
choices.B: The buyer reasonably thought that a dilapidated shed backed up against the fence was to be torn down and removed as part of the agreement, but the seller did not. As later reduced to writing, the agreement said nothing about the shed.
choices.C: The buyer reasonably thought that the price orally agreed upon was $4,500, but the seller did not. As later reduced to writing, the agreement said $5,000.
choices.D: The buyer reasonably thought that two acres beyond the fence were included in the oral agreement but the seller did not. As later reduced to writing, the agreement included the two acres.

questions.explanation:
Availability of reformation as a remedy
Misrepresentation
  • One party makes untrue assertion of fact that is fraudulent or material
  • Adversely affected party justifiably relies on that misrepresentation
Mutual mistake
  • Both parties are mistaken as to contract's contents or legal effect
Unilateral mistake
(from fraudulent
misrepresentation)
  • One party is mistaken because other party intentionally misrepresented contract's content or legal effect
  • Adversely affected party justifiably relies on that misrepresentation

Reformation is an equitable remedy that courts can use to rewrite a contract to reflect the parties' original intent. This remedy is available when a writing that embodies an agreement fails to express the agreement because of a mistake by both parties as to its content or legal effect. When reformation is available to cure a mutual mistake, neither party can avoid the contract.

Here, the parties agreed to the sale and purchase of a 10-acre tract of land and orally marked its bounds, including "the fence on the other side." Due to a clerical mistake, the written agreement included two acres beyond the fence (ie, two acres neither party intended to include as part of the transaction). Therefore, at the request of either party, the court may reform the writing to cure their mutual mistake.

(Choices B, C & D) The buyer and seller did not agree to the same terms, so it would be impossible to reform the writing to reflect their actual agreement. Instead, no contract exists because there was no meeting of the minds.

📌 Educational Objective

A court may reform a contract that fails to accurately express the parties' agreement because of a mistake by both parties as to its content or legal effect.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 155 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (mistake of both parties justifying reformation).
questions.zh-question:
卖方和买方站在一块10英亩的土地上，口头同意以5000美元的价格进行买卖，并口头将其边界标记为“那边的树林、与树林相交的沟渠、另一边的栅栏以及第四边的街道。”

在下列哪种情况中，合同修正 (reformation) 的救济措施最为适当？

zh-choices.A: 之后在拟定书面合同时，由于文书错误，协议包含了实际上在栅栏之外的两英亩土地。
zh-choices.B: 买方合理地认为，作为协议的一部分，那个靠着栅栏的破旧棚屋将被拆除，但卖方并不同意。之后拟定的书面协议对该棚屋只字未提。
zh-choices.C: 买方合理地认为口头约定的价格是4500美元，但卖方并不同意。之后拟定的书面协议写明价格为5000美元。
zh-choices.D: 买方合理地认为栅栏外的两英亩土地包含在口头协议中，但卖方并不同意。之后拟定的书面协议包含了这两英亩土地。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Remedies - Defenses To Formation

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：写成书面合同时，只有“双方都想要的意思”写歪了，法院才会用 重述（reformation） 把文字改回双方原意。

三秒认题路径：

口头已同意 → 书面写歪 → 双方同错 → 可重述 → 选 A

核心法律规则

重述（reformation）是衡平救济，考场意思：不是改交易内容，而是把书面文本改成双方真正谈好的内容。

它适用于 双方共同错误（mutual mistake），也就是书面合同没有准确表达双方对合同内容或法律效果的共同意思。若只有一方想法和另一方不同，就不是“写错了”，而是根本没谈拢。

所以这题只看一个点：书面协议是不是因为共同笔误，把双方都没打算要的两英亩写进去了。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 155 锁定结论：共同错误导致书面不能反映原意时，可以重述。

思维导图

先看：书面合同有没有把双方原本同意的内容写歪？
是，共同写错
口头先定 10 英亩，边界还当场画出来
后来写成文书
多写了 fence 外的两英亩
杀点：双方都没想要那两英亩，属于共同错误，不是谈判分歧。
结果：法院可把书面改回原意 → 选 A
不是，共识就不一致
一方想要、另一方没答应 = 没有 meeting of the minds
杀点：这时不能“重述”出一个根本没谈成的条款。
结论：B、C、D 都是在偷换成“双方没同意同一条款”。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：只要写进合同的文字和一方当初理解不同，就可以改。

但考试真正问的是：双方有没有就这个条款达成同一意思，后来只是书面 clerical mistake 写歪了。

司法考试看的是「书面有没有准确反映双方原意」，而不是「某一方后来觉得不满意」。

所以别被“shed、price、two acres”这些细节带跑；只要不是双方共同想错，就不是重述题，而是没谈成。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干已口头划定边界，后来的书面却因 clerical mistake 多写了 fence 外两英亩；这正是双方共同错误下的重述场景。

❌ 概念混淆 | 条款未达成

✕ B: 把 shed 当成双方共识，其实只是买方单方理解。

❌ 法律适用 | 价格记错

✕ C: 把 $4,500 当成可重述对象，但双方根本没谈成同一价格。

❌ 事实误判 | 方向偷换

✕ D: 把 two acres 说成口头共识，事实正相反。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清“共同写错”还是“各说各话”；只有前者才进 reformation。

考场速记

记住一句：重述（reformation）不是替当事人重新谈判，而是把书面改回双方原来同意的样子；一方想错、另一方没同意，就直接排除。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Determine when contract reformation is appropriate

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A job-search website provided consumers with online access to job openings based upon the consumer's location and specific area of expertise. The website wanted to expand the usefulness of its services, so it hired a production company to produce instructional videos regarding the job-hiring process, ranging from how to write a resume to interviewing tips. The written agreement dated September 20 stipulated that the production company would produce 10 five-minute instructional videos regarding the interview process based upon the general guidelines provided by the website regarding video content. The website agreed to pay $1,500 for each video, provided that the video was in high definition. The contract called for all of the videos to be completed by November 20. Due to issues regarding the availability of video cameras, the production company delivered the 10 videos in standard definition on November 30. Nonetheless, the website used the standard-definition videos, but it refused to pay the production company for its services.
Can the production company recover any damages from the website for providing the 10 videos in standard definition on November 30?

choices.A: No, because the production company breached the contract.
choices.B: No, because the contract contained an express condition that the videos be in high definition.
choices.C: Yes, because the website used the standard-definition videos on its website.
choices.D: Yes, because there was no "time is of the essence" clause in the contract.

questions.explanation:
Restitutionary damages
Definition
  • Damages awarded to restore to claimant the value of whatever benefit was conferred upon recipient
Purpose
  • Prevent unjust enrichment
Measure
  • Reasonable value of work performed or services rendered (ie, cost of recipient obtaining comparable performance)
  • If applicable, extent to which recipient's property has increased in value or recipient's other interests have been advanced

If a plaintiff has not substantially performed and is therefore in breach of a contract, the plaintiff is not typically permitted to recover under the contract. However, if the defendant has benefited from the plaintiff's part performance, then the plaintiff can still generally recover in restitution for the benefit conferred on the defendant minus the defendant's damages for the plaintiff's breach. This is designed to prevent the defendant from being unjustly enriched.

Here, the contract called for the production company to complete 10 videos in high definition by November 20. However, the production company delivered the videos to the website in standard definition on November 30. But because the website chose to use the standard-definition videos anyway, the production company has conferred a benefit on the website and a lack of any recovery would be unjust. Therefore, the production company will be able to recover in restitution for providing the 10 standard-definition videos to prevent unjust enrichment.

(Choice B) If a defendant's obligation to perform is subject to a condition precedent, the plaintiff must prove that the condition occurred to recover under the contract. Here, the production company would have to prove that the videos were in high definition to seek damages under the contract, but not to seek restitution.

(Choices A & D) The plaintiff's late performance of a contract does not automatically prevent recovery under the contract, even if the contract contained a "time is of the essence" clause. And here, even if the production company's delay constituted a breach of the contract, it would not prevent the company from recovering restitution.

📌 Educational Objective

If the defendant has benefited from the plaintiff's part performance, then the plaintiff can still generally recover in restitution for the benefit conferred on the defendant minus the defendant's damages for the plaintiff's breach.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 370 (Am. L. Inst. 1981) (providing that a party is entitled to restitution only to the extent that he has conferred a benefit on the other party by way of part performance or reliance).
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 374 (Am. L. Inst. 1981) (providing the measure of restitution damages for a party in breach).

一家求职网站为消费者提供基于其所在位置和特定专业领域的在线职位空缺信息。该网站希望扩大其服务的实用性，于是雇用了一家制作公司制作有关求职录用流程的教学视频，内容从如何写简历到面试技巧不等。日期为9月20日的书面协议规定，制作公司应根据网站就视频内容提供的一般指导，制作10个每个5分钟的关于面试过程的教学视频。网站同意就每个视频支付1,500美元，但前提是视频必须为 high definition（高清）。合同要求所有视频须在11月20日前完成。由于摄像机可用性方面出现问题，制作公司于11月30日交付了10个 standard definition（标清）视频。尽管如此，网站使用了这些标清视频，但拒绝向制作公司支付服务费用。

制作公司能否就其于11月30日提供这10个标清视频而向网站追回任何 damages（损害赔偿）？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为制作公司构成了合同违约。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为合同包含一项明示条件，即视频必须为 high definition（高清）。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为网站在其网站上使用了这些标清视频。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为合同中没有“time is of the essence（时间至关重要）”条款。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Remedies - Reliance & restitution interests

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：违约方提供了有价值的部分履行，如果对方真的用了这个好处，违约方还能不能拿到返还性损害赔偿（restitution）来防止不当得利（unjust enrichment）。

三秒认题路径：

违约先别慌 → 对方是否受益 → 是否实际使用 → 返还求偿 → 选能

核心法律规则

返还性损害赔偿（restitution）的考场意思：不是按合同价硬算，而是看对方到底拿到了多少好处。部分履行（part performance）后，即使履行方自己先违约，只要对方确实受益，法院通常仍允许按受益价值追偿。这里的关键不是“有没有晚”，而是“对方有没有白拿好处”。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts §§ 370, 374 — 说明违约方只要确实给对方带来利益，仍可就该利益请求返还，金额以受益价值扣除对方损失为准。

思维导图

1. 先看谁得利
网站用了标准清晰版视频，说明它不是“没收货”，而是真的拿去用了。
2. 再看履行形态
制作方交的是标准清晰度（standard definition），没做到约定的高清，但仍提供了可用成果。
3. 关卡：返还而非合同价
既然对方已经使用，就会触发返还（restitution）逻辑：防止网站把视频拿走却一分钱不付。
4. 卡死结论
对方已使用 = 有利益 = 可追返还

考点陷阱

你可能会想：制作方自己晚交、还没做到高清，所以应该直接输。
但考试真正问的是：网站有没有白拿到可用视频，还拒绝付任何对价。
司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 website used the standard-definition videos，说明它确实受益；制作方即便违约，也能就该利益主张返还性损害赔偿（restitution）。

❌ 概念混淆 | 违约即全输

✕ A: 把breached当成“永远不能要回钱”。

❌ 法律适用 | 条件混成合同价

✕ B: 盯着high definition就以为只能按合同条件死卡，忽略了返还救济。

❌ 事实误判 | 晚交放大误读

✕ D: 没有time is of the essence，不等于不能因为受益而返还。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看对方有没有实际受益，再判断是否进入返还，而不是先被“自己违约”吓退。

考场速记

记住一句：“对方拿到好处，就可能要返还；自己先违约，不等于对方可以白拿。” 这题的核心不是合同价，而是有没有不当得利（unjust enrichment）。
口诀：先问“谁得利”，再问“该不该还”。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A homeowner and a contractor entered into a contract for the construction of a home for $300,000. The contractor was to earn a profit of $10,000 for the job. After the contractor had spent $45,000 on labor and materials, including $5,000 on oak flooring not yet installed, the homeowner informed the contractor that the homeowner had lost her job and could not pay the contractor for his services. The homeowner told the contractor to stop working immediately.
The reasonable market value of the labor and materials provided by the contractor at that point, including the oak flooring, was $40,000. The contractor used the oak flooring on another job.
In an action by the contractor against the homeowner for damages, which of the following would be the largest amount of damages recoverable by the contractor?

choices.A: $40,000, the contractor's construction costs.
choices.B: $40,000, the reasonable value of the services the contractor had provided.
choices.C: $50,000, the contractor's construction costs of $45,000 plus the $10,000 profit minus the $5,000 saved by reusing the oak flooring on another job.
choices.D: $55,000, the contractor's construction costs of $45,000 plus the $10,000 profit.

questions.explanation:
Compensatory damages for breach of construction contracts
Before construction starts During construction After construction completed
Breach by builder
(owner paid) 		Owner entitled to cost of completion Owner entitled to:
  • cost of completion/correction if no undue economic waste OR
  • value of promised construction minus nonconforming construction
 N/A
Breach by owner
(did not pay) 		Builder entitled to:
  • lost profits plus costs incurred OR
  • contract price minus cost of completion
 Builder entitled to contract price

Compensatory damages are intended to place the nonbreaching party in the same position as if the contract had been performed (ie, give that party the benefit of the bargain). Where an owner breaches a construction contract before or during construction, the builder is entitled to recover the profits it would have earned had the contract been completed plus costs incurred up to that point. However, any costs saved or otherwise avoided (ie, mitigated) by the builder will be subtracted to arrive at the final damages award.

Here, the contractor had spent $45,000 on labor and materials when the homeowner stopped the work. And the contractor had expected to make a $10,000 profit for this job. As a result, he would be entitled to recover $55,000 except that he saved $5,000 by using the oak flooring on another job. Therefore, the largest amount of damages recoverable by the contractor is $50,000 ($10,000 expected profit + $45,000 costs incurred - $5,000 costs saved) (Choice C).

(Choice A) The contractor's $40,000 construction costs ($45,000 costs incurred - $5,000 costs saved) represent his reliance damages—ie, damages intended to place the injured party in the same position as if the contract had never been entered. But this measure of recovery fails to account for the contractor's $10,000 anticipated profit.

(Choice B) Restitution damages are measured by the benefit conferred on another party. But here, the $40,000 amount (reasonable value of the services the contractor had provided) is an incorrect measure of restitution damages since it fails to deduct the $5,000 worth of oak flooring the contractor used on another job. $35,000 would be the correct measure, and this represents the smallest amount of recoverable damages.

📌 Educational Objective

When an owner breaches a construction contract before or during construction, the builder's damages are equal to the builder's lost profits plus costs incurred, minus any costs saved or otherwise avoided.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 344 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (purpose of remedies).
questions.zh-question:
一位房主与一位承包商签订了一份价值30万美元的房屋建造合同。承包商将从此项工作中获得1万美元的利润。在承包商已花费4.5万美元用于劳务和材料（其中包括5000美元尚未安装的橡木地板）后，房主告知承包商她已失业，无法支付其服务费用。房主让承包商立即停工。

当时，承包商所提供的劳务和材料（包括橡木地板）的合理市场价值为4万美元。承包商将橡木地板用于另一项工作。

在承包商对房主提起的损害赔偿诉讼中，承包商可获得的最高赔偿金额是下列哪一项？

zh-choices.A: $40,000，承包商的建造成本。
zh-choices.B: $40,000，承包商已提供服务的合理价值。
zh-choices.C: $50,000，即承包商的建造成本45,000美元加上10,000美元的利润，再减去因将橡木地板用于另一项工作而节省的5,000美元。
zh-choices.D: $55,000，即承包商的建造成本45,000美元加上10,000美元的利润。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Remedies - Remedies

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：发包人先违约时，承包人能拿到的是期待利益（expectation damages），也就是已发生成本（costs incurred）加上预期利润（lost profits），再减去已经省掉或转用掉的成本。

三秒认题路径：

业主先停工 → 建筑合同 → 承包人求赔 → 已花成本+利润 → 减去节省成本

核心法律规则

期待利益（expectation damages）就是把守约方放回“合同照做完后本来应有的位置”，所以不是只赔成本，也不是只看对方得了多少好处。

在建设合同（construction contract）里，如果业主（owner）在施工中途先违约，承包人（builder）通常可以要预期利润（lost profits） + 已经发生的合理成本，再扣掉任何已节省/已避免成本（costs saved or avoided）。

这里的关键不是“我花了多少”，而是“如果你不毁约，我本来能赚多少”；考试只要看到业主中途叫停，通常就先想这个公式。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 344 - 说明赔偿目标是让守约方拿到“合同本来该给他的利益”。

思维导图

1. 先看谁先违约
题干事实：homeowner told the contractor to stop working，是业主先毁约。
2. 选赔偿模型
承包人走期待利益（expectation），不是只算成本，也不是只算对方受益。
3. 公式直接套
已花成本 $45,000 + 预期利润 $10,000 - 已节省成本 $5,000。
4. 别被成本骗走
只报 $40,000 会漏掉利润；只报 $55,000 会漏掉减损。
5. 终点
所以最大可赔 = $50,000，对应正确选项。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然承包人实际花了 $45,000，那就只赔成本最稳。

但考试真正问的是：业主先毁约后，承包人要拿的是合同利益，不是把账本里“花出去的钱”机械抄回来。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干给出已支出 $45,000、预期利润 $10,000，再扣掉转用木地板省下的 $5,000，所以最高可赔 $50,000。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 你把reliance当成全部赔偿了，漏掉了利润。

❌ 事实误判 | 价值口径偷换

✕ B: 你把reasonable value当成答案，但题目要的是合同违约损害，不是单算服务价值。

❌ 法律适用 | 少扣减损失误判

✕ D: 你只加了profit和成本，忘了减去转用材料省下的 $5,000。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓违约方是谁，再直接套“已发生成本 + 预期利润 - 已节省成本”的公式。

考场速记

记住这句：业主先停工时，承包人的标准答案通常是利润 + 已发生成本 - 已避免成本，不是只报成本，也不是只报市场价值。

question_analysis.skill_tested: apply construction contract expectation damages formula

keywords.text: contract for the construction of a home

reason.en: Identifies the contract type, which governs the specific formula used to calculate expectation damages.
reason.zh: 确定合同类型，这决定了计算期望利益赔偿所使用的特定公式。

reason.en: Represents the net profit component of the contractor's expectation interest.

reason.en: Represents the builder's performance costs incurred prior to the owner's breach.

reason.en: The homeowner's instruction that constitutes a total breach, halting performance and locking in damages.

keywords.text: used the oak flooring on another job

reason.en: Indicates cost savings that must be deducted from expectation damages to prevent double recovery.
reason.zh: 表明必须从期望利益赔偿中扣除的成本节省，以防止双重赔偿。

reason.en: Represents reliance damages minus mitigated flooring costs, but fails to include the expected profit.
reason.zh: 代表扣除已减损地板成本后的信赖损害赔偿，但未能包含预期利润。

B.text: $40,000, the reasonable value of the services the contractor had provided.

label.zh: 恢复原状/量子受益赔偿干扰项

reason.en: Incorrectly applies quantum meruit/restitution value without accounting for expectation profit or mitigated materials.

C.text: $50,000, the contractor's construction costs of $45,000 plus the $10,000 profit minus the $5,000 saved by reusing the oak flooring on another job.

reason.en: Correctly calculates expectation damages by adding expected profits to costs incurred and deducting avoided costs.

D.text: $55,000, the contractor's construction costs of $45,000 plus the $10,000 profit.

reason.zh: 未能扣除承包商避免的成本（重新利用地板节省的$5,000），导致过度赔偿。

highlights.text: contractor was to earn a profit of $10,000

reason.en: Provides the expected profit value that is added under the expectation damages formula.
reason.zh: 提供了在期望利益损害赔偿公式下应加入的预期利润值。

highlights.text: spent $45,000 on labor and materials

reason.en: Provides the incurred costs value that is added under the expectation damages formula.
reason.zh: 提供了在期望利益损害赔偿公式下应加入的已支出成本值。

highlights.text: contractor used the oak flooring on another job.

reason.en: Indicates mitigation of costs, which must be subtracted from the expectation damages total.
reason.zh: 指示了损失的减轻，这必须从期望利益赔偿总额中扣除。

highlights.text: largest amount of damages recoverable by the contractor?

reason.en: Directs the selection of expectation damages as the maximum contract damages measure giving the benefit of the bargain.

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.topic: Remedies: Damages For Breach Of Contract
questions.question:
The owner of a house and a real estate investor signed a writing in which the owner, "in consideration of $100 to be paid to the owner by the investor," offered the investor the right to purchase the house for $100,000 within 30 days. The writing further provided, "This offer will become effective as an option only if and when the $100 consideration is in fact paid."
Two weeks later, the owner, having received no payment or other communication from the investor, sold and conveyed the house to the investor's business rival for $120,000. The following day, the owner received a letter from the investor enclosing a cashier's check for $100 payable to the owner and stating, "I am hereby exercising my option to purchase the house and am prepared to close whenever you're ready."
Assume that, for whatever reason, the investor prevails in a suit against the owner for breach of contract.
Which of the following is the investor entitled to recover?

choices.A: $20,000, plus the amount, if any, by which the fair market value of the house on the date of the owner's breach exceeded $120,000.
choices.B: Nominal damages only, because the remedy of specific performance was not available to the investor.
choices.C: The amount, if any, by which the fair market value of the house on the date of the owner's breach exceeded $100,000.
choices.D: The fair market value, if any, of an assignable option to purchase the house for $100,000.

questions.explanation:
Buyer's recovery of expectation damages

Land's fair market value at time of breach
Contract price
Lost expectation damages

A buyer who enters a contract for the sale of land expects to receive the property (worth its fair market value) in exchange for the contract price. If the seller breaches by refusing to sell, the buyer can recover for loss of bargain (ie, lost expectation), which amounts to the property's fair market value on the date of the breach minus the contract price.

Here, the real estate investor paid $100 for the option to buy the owner's house for $100,000. The investor exercised this option, and the owner breached the resulting land-sales contract since he had already sold the house to the business rival. Therefore, the investor is entitled to recover for his lost expectation, which is the amount, if any, by which the fair market value of the house on the date of the breach exceeded $100,000.

(Choice A) Although the owner sold the house to the business rival for $20,000 more than the investor had agreed to pay, the investor cannot automatically recover that $20,000. This is because the investor's expectation is based on his own contract price—not the business rival's.

(Choice B) Nominal damages (eg, $1) can be awarded for breach when there was no substantial loss—not because specific performance is unavailable. Here, the investor likely did suffer a substantial loss since, based on the business rival's $120,000 payment, the fair market value of the house likely exceeded $100,000.

(Choice D) Options are generally assignable (ie, transferable). But the damages for breaching an option are equal to the lost expectation of the nonbreaching party—which is distinct from (and likely greater than) the fair market value of the assignable option itself.

📌 Educational Objective

When a seller breaches a land-sales contract by refusing to sell the property to the buyer, the buyer can recover for loss of bargain—ie, the fair market value of the property on the date of the breach minus the contract price.

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 347 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (explaining that a nonbreaching party's lost expectation is equal to the loss in value to him/her caused by the other party's failure to perform).

一位房屋所有人和一位房地产投资者签署了一份书面文件，该文件中，房屋所有人“以投资者将支付给所有人的100美元为对价”，向投资者发出要约，给予其在30天内以100,000美元购买该房屋的权利。该书面文件进一步规定，“只有当100美元的对价实际支付后，该要约才作为一项期权生效。”

两周后，房屋所有人在未收到投资者任何付款或其他通知的情况下，以120,000美元的价格将房屋出售并转让给了该投资者的商业竞争对手。第二天，房屋所有人收到了投资者的一封信，内附一张支付给所有人的100美元银行本票，信中写道：“我在此行使我的购房期权，并准备好随时完成交易。”

假设，无论出于何种原因，投资者在对房屋所有人提起的违约诉讼中胜诉。

投资者有权获得以下哪项赔偿？

zh-choices.A: 20,000美元，加上在房屋所有人违约之日，房屋公平市价超出120,000美元的部分（如有）。
zh-choices.B: 仅象征性损害赔偿，因为投资者无法获得实际履行救济。
zh-choices.C: 在房屋所有人违约之日，房屋公平市价超出100,000美元的部分（如有）。
zh-choices.D: 一项可转让的、以100,000美元购买该房屋的期权的公平市价（如有）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Remedies - Remedies: Damages For Breach Of Contract

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：土地买卖中，卖方毁约后买方能拿多少 期待利益损害赔偿（expectation damages），核心就是 市价 - 合同价（fair market value minus contract price）。

三秒认题路径：

卖方毁约 → 土地买卖 → 买方期待利益 → fair market value − 合同价 → 选 C

核心法律规则

规则只抓这条

在土地买卖合同（contract for the sale of land）里，买方买到的是房子的价值，不是对方后来转卖赚了多少，所以赔偿看的是房子在违约日的 市价（fair market value） 减去买方合同价。

这里 违约（breach） 发生在卖方已经把房子卖给第三人、导致买方不能取得房子的时候；买方一旦已正确行使 期权（option），后面就进入普通的土地买卖违约赔偿逻辑。

核心判例： Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 347 — 期待利益就是“因对方不履行而少拿到的价值”。

思维导图

先看买方到底要什么：房子本身，不是转卖利润。
1. 卖方把房子卖给第三人后，买方失去的是 期待利益（expectation interest）。
2. 计算公式只看：违约日市价 − 合同价。
3. 题干的 $120,000 只是第三人出价，能提示市价可能高于 $100,000，但不能直接让买方拿 $20,000。
卡死点：effective reviewable 这种想法不属于本题；这里直接卡在“买方自己的合同价”。
4. 所以损害赔偿 = 房屋违约日市价 超过 $100,000 的部分。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：卖给第三人多赚了 $20,000，所以买方就该拿这 $20,000。

但考试真正问的是：买方自己的 期待利益，不是卖方后来卖得更贵带来的“额外利润”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题的坑在于把“第三人出价”偷换成“买方损失”；真正的损失是买方本来能用 $100,000 买到的房子，现在因为违约没拿到的那部分价值。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干已经说明卖方先把房子卖掉，买方只能按违约日市价高于 $100,000 的部分索赔；期待利益只看买方自己的合同价。

❌ 事实误判 | 转售价偷换

✕ A: 把第三人的 $120,000 当成买方当然损失了。

❌ 法律适用 | 救济条件错位

✕ B: 把 specific performance 不可得当成只能拿名义赔偿。

❌ 概念混淆 | 期权价值混同

✕ D: 把 assignable option 的市场价误当成全部赔偿。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定买方合同价，再用“违约日市价减合同价”直接算，不要被第三人转售价带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：土地违约赔偿 = 违约日市价 − 买方合同价；别拿卖给别人赚了多少来算，算的是买方少拿到多少。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.question:
A landowner contracted in a signed writing to sell a 500-acre tract of farmland to a farmer. The contract provided for exchange of the deed and purchase price of $500,000 in cash on January 15. Possession was to be given to the farmer on the same date.
On January 15, the landowner notified the farmer that because the tenant on the farmland wrongfully refused to quit the premises until January 30, the landowner would be unable to deliver possession of the farmland until then, but he assured the farmer that he would tender the deed and possession on that date. When the landowner tendered the deed and possession on January 30, the farmer refused to accept either, and refused to pay the $500,000. Throughout the month of January, the market value of the farmland was $510,000, and its fair monthly rental value was $5,000.
Will the landowner likely succeed in an action against the farmer for specific performance?

choices.A: No, because the landowner breached by failing to tender the deed and possession on January 15.
choices.B: No, because the landowner's remedy at law for monetary relief is adequate.
choices.C: Yes, because the court will excuse the delay in tender on the ground that there was a temporary impossibility caused by the tenant's holding over.
choices.D: Yes, because time is ordinarily not of the essence in a land-sale contract.

questions.explanation:
Seller's remedies
Rescission &
restitution
  • Rescind (ie, cancel) agreement & recover possession of property
  • Rental value & physical damages are recoverable
  • Buyer not liable for purchase price
Specific
performance
  • Seek an injunction ordering buyer to pay agreed purchase price
  • May be unavailable if money damages provide adequate compensation & property is not unique
  • ◦ eg, condominium identical to other units in complex
Damages
  • Loss of bargain = contract price − market value at time of breach
  • Liquidated damages = amount designated in the sales contract as compensation for breach
  • Retain buyer's deposit (up to amount of seller's actual damages)
  • Incidental & consequential damages that were contemplated during sales contract or reasonably foreseeable

In a land-sale contract, the seller is required to deliver marketable title to the buyer at the closing date. Failure to do so constitutes a breach of the contract. But if the seller conveys the land within a reasonable time after the closing date, the buyer cannot withhold payment. That is because time is ordinarily not of the essence in a land-sale contract unless the circumstances indicate that performance by that date is important.

Here, the landowner breached the contract by failing to tender the deed and possession of the farm to the farmer on January 15 (closing date). But the landowner did so on January 30 (reasonable time after closing). The circumstances do not indicate that time was of the essence, so the farmer breached the contract by refusing to pay the purchase price (Choice A).

A seller's potential remedies for a buyer's breach include specific performance, which allows the court to issue an injunction that orders the buyer to pay the agreed purchase price. Specific performance is appropriate when monetary damages are inadequate (eg, unique land). Farms are unique since each has different characteristics. Therefore, the landowner can obtain specific performance as a remedy against the farmer (Choice B).

(Choice C) Performance is discharged (ie, excused) when an unexpected and extraordinary event beyond the parties' control makes performance impossible. Here, the landowner should have known that the tenant on the farmland could hold over. As a result, the landowner's delay is not excused due to impossibility.

📌 Educational Objective

Time is ordinarily not of the essence in a contract for the sale of land, so the buyer cannot withhold payment if the seller conveys the land within a reasonable time after closing. If the buyer breaches by refusing to pay, the seller can obtain specific performance when monetary damages would be inadequate (eg, unique land).

📚 References
  • Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 242 (Am. Law Inst. 1981) (effect of delayed performance).
  • 77 Am. Jur. 2d Vendor and Purchaser § 445 (2020) (seller's remedies).
questions.zh-question:
【合同法——救济】

一位土地所有人以签署书面合同的方式，将一块500英亩的农田出售给一位农民。合同约定于1月15日交换契据（deed）与50万美元现金购价，并在同一天将占有（possession）交付给该农民。

1月15日，土地所有人通知农民：由于农田上的承租人（tenant）错误地拒绝在1月30日之前腾退该房地（quit the premises），土地所有人将无法在1月15日之前交付该农田的占有，但他保证会在1月30日交付契据和占有。1月30日，土地所有人交付契据并提出交付占有时，农民拒绝接受任何一项，也拒绝支付50万美元。整个1月份，该农田的市场价值为51万美元，其公平月租金价值为5,000美元。

土地所有人是否可能在针对该农民请求特定履行（specific performance）的诉讼中胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为土地所有人未能在1月15日交付契据和占有，构成违约。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为土地所有人可在法律上获得金钱赔偿的救济已足够。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为法院会以承租人逾期占有（holding over）造成的暂时性履行不能（temporary impossibility）为由，原谅该迟延交付。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为在土地买卖合同中，时间通常不被视为合同的要素（time is ordinarily not of the essence）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Remedies - Specific Performance

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：卖方在土地买卖合同里，买方能否因卖方迟延交付而拒付价款，以及卖方能否拿到特定履行（specific performance）。

三秒认题路径：

土地买卖 → 迟延交付 → 时间非要件 → 买方先违约 → 卖方可求特定履行

核心法律规则

在土地买卖合同（land-sale contract）里，时间通常不是要件（time is not of the essence），所以卖方如果在合理时间内补交地契和交付占有，买方一般不能借“晚了几天”就拒付价款，考场意思：先看是不是还在可接受的迟延窗口里。

如果买方拒付，卖方的救济可以是特定履行（specific performance），因为土地通常被视为独特标的，金钱赔偿不一定够，考场意思：地块不只是“值多少钱”，而是“这块地本身”很难替代。

所谓不可替代损害（money damages inadequate），不是说卖方一点钱都拿不到，而是说钱不能把结果补回来得足够好，所以法院才会逼买方按合同付钱并完成交易。

核心判例： 本题对应 Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 242 的思路：土地迟延交付若仍属合理时间，买方不能直接翻桌拒付；卖方可用特定履行逼买方履约。

思维导图

先看：卖方有没有在“合理时间内”补交？
有 合同是土地买卖，时间通常不是要件（time not of the essence）。
所以 买方不能因为1月15日没交、1月30日才交就当然拒付。
再看：买方拒付后，卖方要什么？
规则 卖方可求特定履行（specific performance），逼买方支付约定价款。
为什么 500英亩农地通常有独特性，金钱赔偿不够，第三要件过关。
干扰点：租户赖着不走 = 不可抗力吗？
不算 这类持有不走是卖方应当预见的风险，不会自动免除迟延。
结论 正确答案：D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：卖方1月15日没法立刻交房交地，应该已经先违约了。

但考试真正问的是：土地买卖里时间通常不是要件，卖方在合理时间内补交后，买方不能用这个理由直接拒付。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的拖延看起来有多麻烦」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干显示卖方在1月30日合理时间内补交，占有与地契都已可履行；在土地买卖中，时间通常不是要件，所以买方拒付后，卖方可请求特定履行。

❌ 事实误判 | 逾期即毁约

✕ A: 把January 15当成绝对死线，忽略合理迟延。

❌ 法律适用 | 金钱救济误判

✕ B: 看到monetary relief就只想钱，忘了土地独特性。

❌ 概念混淆 | 不可抗力套错

✕ C: 把租户赖走当成temporary impossibility，但这不是免责理由。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓土地合同的时间规则，再看买方拒付后卖方能否用特定履行锁住交易。

考场速记

记住这句：土地买卖里，时间通常不是要件；卖方在合理时间内补交后，买方别急着拒付，卖方还能靠特定履行（specific performance）把交易逼完。

买方想立刻上诉式“翻案”不行，先问：是不是土地、是不是合理迟延、是不是独特标的。time is not of the essence 是这题的钥匙。

questions.subject: Contracts
questions.topic: Remedies: Damages For Breach Of Contract
questions.question:
A bakery contracted with a mill to provide 10,000 pounds of flour for $100,000. Prior to the date fixed for delivery of the flour, the mill, without justification, informed the bakery that it could not supply the flour. The bakery immediately sought and received a quote from a second source, who previously provided the bakery with flour in a timely and satisfactory manner. This source agreed to sell 10,000 pounds of flour for $120,000. Shortly after that, the bakery received a quote from a third source, who previously failed to deliver a promised order of flour to the bakery. The third source agreed to supply 10,000 pounds of flour for $100,000. Reasonably concerned that the third source would not provide the flour in a timely and satisfactory manner, the bakery contracted with the second source. Subsequently, the mill told the bakery that it could supply the flour by the original delivery date and provided the bakery with adequate evidence that the flour would be timely delivered. The bakery told the mill not to deliver the flour, instead acquiring it from the second source. The bakery sued the mill for $20,000.
Can the mill successfully defend against this action?

choices.A: No, because the bakery is entitled to recover the cost of acquiring substitute flour.
choices.B: No, because the mill lost the opportunity to supply the flour as soon as it repudiated its promise to deliver the flour.
choices.C: Yes, because the bakery was required to mitigate its damages by accepting the third source's lower offer.
choices.D: Yes, because the mill withdrew its repudiation prior to the time for performance.

questions.explanation:
UCC damages for seller's breach when buyer covers
Cost of cover
  • Difference between contract price & cost of purchasing substitute goods*
Incidental damages
  • Reasonable expenses incurred in inspection, receipt, transportation & care of goods rightfully rejected
  • Commercially reasonable charges, expenses, or commissions incurred in connection with effecting cover
  • Other reasonable expenses incident to delay/breach
Consequential
damages
  • Losses resulting from buyer's particular circumstances that:
    • seller had reason to know at time of contracting and
    • could not reasonably be prevented
  • Injury to person/property proximately resulting from breach of warranty
UCC = Uniform Commercial Code.
*The substitute goods must have been purchased promptly & in good faith.

Under the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC), when the seller clearly and unequivocally repudiates before the time for performance is due, the buyer may:

  • treat the anticipatory repudiation as a breach and sue the seller immediately or
  • ignore the anticipatory repudiation and demand performance.

Among the remedies available to a buyer who chooses to treat the anticipatory repudiation as a breach is to buy substitute goods (i.e., cover) and recover the replacement price minus the contract price.

Here, the mill clearly and unequivocally repudiated the contract by informing the bakery that it could not supply the flour. This gave the bakery the right to treat the anticipatory repudiation as a breach and cover by acquiring flour from another source. The bakery can now recover $20,000, the difference between the contract price ($100,000) and the cost of the substitute flour ($120,000). Therefore, the mill cannot successfully defend against this action.

(Choice B) A party who anticipatorily repudiates a contractual obligation may nevertheless retract the repudiation and perform as promised. Here, the mill could have retracted its repudiation had the bakery not found an alternative flour source in the intervening period.

(Choice C) Although a party is required to mitigate its damages, a party does not have to do so if it would involve undue risk. Here, accepting the third source's lower offer would involve undue risk because the source previously failed to deliver a promised order of flour to the bakery.

(Choice D) Repudiation may be retracted, but not if the other party has materially changed position in reliance on the repudiation. And here, the bakery entered into a contract with the second source before the mill attempted to retract its repudiation.

📌 Educational Objective

When a seller breaches a contract through anticipatory repudiation and the buyer chooses to cover, the buyer can recover the difference between the replacement price and the contract price.

📚 References
  • U.C.C. § 2-610 (describing the doctrine of anticipatory repudiation).
  • U.C.C. § 2-712 (explaining that a buyer has the right to cover when the seller breaches the contract).
questions.zh-question:
主题：Contracts — Remedies

题目：
一家面包店与一家磨坊签订合同，由磨坊以100,000美元提供10,000磅面粉。在约定交付面粉的日期之前，磨坊在没有正当理由的情况下通知面包店其无法供货。面包店立即向第二个来源询价，该来源此前曾按时且令人满意地向面包店供应过面粉。该来源同意以120,000美元出售10,000磅面粉。不久之后，面包店又收到第三个来源的报价。该第三个来源此前曾未能向面包店交付一笔承诺的面粉订单。第三个来源同意以100,000美元供应10,000磅面粉。由于合理担心第三个来源不会按时且令人满意地供货，面包店最终与第二个来源签约。随后，磨坊告诉面包店其可以在原定交货日期前供货，并提供了充分证据证明面粉将会按时交付。面包店告知磨坊无需交付该面粉，而是从第二个来源购买。面包店起诉磨坊，要求赔偿20,000美元。
磨坊能否成功抗辩该诉讼？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为面包店有权追回获得替代面粉（substitute flour）的成本。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为磨坊一旦明示拒绝履行其交付面粉的承诺，就失去了供货的机会。
zh-choices.C: 可以，因为面包店本应通过接受第三个来源更低的报价来减轻损失（mitigate its damages）。
zh-choices.D: 可以，因为磨坊在履行期限到来之前撤回了其拒绝履行（repudiation）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Contracts: Remedies - Remedies: Damages For Breach Of Contract

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：卖方在交货前明确拒绝履行后，买方选择 补进（cover） 时，能否直接按 替代采购价 - 合同价 向卖方索赔。

三秒认题路径：

先拒绝履行 → 再找替代货 → 选了cover → 算价差 → 卖方输

核心法律规则

在《UCC》里，卖方在履行期到来前明确表示不供货，就是 预期违约（anticipatory repudiation），考场意思：买方不用傻等。买方补进（cover） 后，可以要回 替代货价格 - 合同价，考场意思：只看你多花了多少钱。

卖方后来想撤回拒绝履行，也来不及了，如果买方已经因为这个拒绝去找了替代来源并改变了位置。这里 bakery 已经跟第二家签约，所以 mill 不能靠“我又能供了”翻盘。

核心判例： U.C.C. § 2-610 + U.C.C. § 2-712 —— 先有明确预期违约，后有及时善意的 cover，买方就按差价拿赔偿。

思维导图

卖方先说“我不供了”吗？
YES 这是 预期违约（anticipatory repudiation），买方可以立刻把它当成违约处理。
买方有没有 cover？
YES 去买替代货，而且要 及时、善意。
结果：赔 120,000 - 100,000 = 20,000，卖方不能用事后反悔抗辩。
NO 如果不是明确拒绝履行，就回到普通违约分析，不走本题这条线。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：第三家报价也是 100,000，那 bakery 应该接受更便宜的货来减少损失。

但考试真正问的是：买方要不要接受一个自己有理由担心会迟到、会出问题的来源；题干已经告诉你第三家以前失信过，所以 bakery 不用冒这个险。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

mill 先明确拒绝供货，bakery 随后善意 cover，因此可直接追回 20,000 的替代采购差价。

❌ 概念混淆 | 失权时点误判

✕ B: 把“先拒绝”误当成永远不能撤回。

❌ 事实误判 | 低价来源误信

✕ C: 只看 lower offer，却漏掉第三家有迟延前科。

❌ 法律适用 | 撤回条件误套

✕ D: 题干里 bakery 已经先跟第二家签了，mill 的撤回太晚。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓 预期违约，再看买方是否已 cover，最后只算差价。

考场速记

记忆口诀：卖方先拒绝，买方就能 cover；赔偿先看 替代价 - 合同价，别被“后来又能供货”带偏。

question_analysis.skill_tested: evaluating retraction of anticipatory repudiation

keywords.text: informed the bakery that it could not supply the flour

reason.en: Establishes a repudiation of the contract before the delivery date.
reason.zh: 在交货日前确立了对合同的预期违约。

reason.en: Constitutes a material change of position that bars retraction of repudiation.
reason.zh: 构成阻碍撤回预期违约的重大地位改变。

reason.en: Relates to the mill's attempt to retract its repudiation.
reason.zh: 与磨坊试图撤回其预期违约有关。

label.zh: 诉请替代交易损害赔偿

reason.en: Defines the remedy sought by the buyer based on cover cost.
reason.zh: 界定了买方基于替代交易成本所寻求的救济。

A.text: recover the cost of acquiring substitute flour

reason.en: Correctly identifies the buyer's entitlement to cover damages under the UCC.
reason.zh: 正确识别了买方根据UCC获得替代交易损害赔偿的权利。

B.text: lost the opportunity to supply the flour as soon as it repudiated its promise to deliver the flour

reason.en: Incorrectly claims that repudiation alone immediately and irrevocably terminates retraction rights.
reason.zh: 错误地声称单是预期违约行为就立即且不可撤销地终止了撤回权。

C.text: mitigate its damages by accepting the third source's lower offer

reason.en: Misapplies the mitigation rule by forcing dealings with an unreliable party.
reason.zh: 通过强迫与不可信赖的第三方交易，错误地适用了减损规则。

D.text: withdrew its repudiation prior to the time for performance

reason.en: Fails to recognize that retraction is barred once the other party covers.
reason.zh: 未能认识到一旦另一方进行了替代交易，撤回即被阻却。

highlights.text: contracted with the second source

reason.en: Entering a contract with a second source is a material change of position that makes the repudiation final and retraction impossible.
reason.zh: 与第二个来源签订合同属于重大的地位改变，使预期违约成为最终决定且无法撤回。

highlights.text: Subsequently, the mill told the bakery that it could supply the flour by the original delivery date

reason.en: Triggers the rule on retraction of anticipatory repudiation.
reason.zh: 触发了关于撤回预期违约的规则。

highlights.text: The bakery sued the mill for $20,000.

reason.en: Represents the damage claim for the difference between the cover price ($120,000) and the contract price ($100,000).
reason.zh: 代表替代交易价格（120,000美元）与合同价格（100,000美元）之间差额的损害赔偿诉求。
